To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
wireless FD and HFD can significantly improve the communication performance of FL and that over the air computing can be a viable alternative to separate source channel coding.
wireless implementations can be more energy-efficient than their digital counterparts, and that HFD can be more energy efficient than FD.
wireless federated learning is feasible, but the wireless channel can significantly impact performance, especially for federated distillation and hybrid federated distillation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following aspects: (1) Theoretical analysis of the performance of wireless FD and HFD schemes, (2) The design and evaluation of practical implementations of these schemes.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HFD is the best option for distributed learning in wireless networks.
the wireless channel is not an impediment to FL/FD, and that the HFD scheme can achieve a better trade-off between accuracy and energy efficiency.
the wireless implementations of the three schemes are all feasible and that the performance of the HFD scheme is comparable to that of the FD scheme, while both schemes outperform the FL scheme.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed HFD scheme can achieve the same accuracy with 2x less communication compared to FL and 4x less compared to FD.
, while the wireless implementation of FL and FD can be made to work, the wireless implementation of HFD requires further study.

the wireless implementation of FL, FD, and HFD is possible and that wireless FD outperforms wireless FL in the presence of channel noise, but that wireless HFD outperforms both in the presence of data heterogeneity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of a wireless communication channel can significantly affect the performance of FL and FD.
the proposed HFD scheme is able to outperform the FL and FD schemes in terms of the average test error, while maintaining the same communication cost.
, while digital implementations can be more accurate, joint source channel coding can significantly reduce communication costs.
